docs.title: Create a Join Token
docs.text:
This path returns a token that lets one node join the cluster, once.

Method Path POST /api/v1/cluster/tokens

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description ttl_seconds int No Validity of the token, 300 to 86400. Default 1800.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "AXsiaWQiOiI0ZjJk...",
        "expires_at": "2026-11-05T09:44:02Z"
    }
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 The token. 400 ttl_seconds is out of range. 409 The node has no cluster block. 410 The node was removed from the cluster.

docs.title: Join a Cluster
docs.text:
This path joins a node with no user to a cluster. It takes no access token.

Method Path POST /api/v1/cluster/join

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description token string Yes A token from Create a Join Token.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "token": "AXsiaWQiOiI0ZjJk..."
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Joined the cluster"
    }
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 The token is not valid or expired, or the node runs an older version than the cluster. 403 The node has a user. 409 The node is already in a cluster, or has no cluster block, the token was used, or a peer or another member has the node's Diameter host. 429 Too many attempts from the client address. 502 No member answered.

docs.title: Update a Member
docs.text:
This path sets the display name of a member.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description display_name string Yes Up to 63 bytes. Empty clears it.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "display_name": "paris-1"
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 The name is over 63 bytes. 404 No such member. 410 The node was removed from the cluster.

docs.title: Drain a Member
docs.text:
Method Path POST /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}/drain POST /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}/resume

drain sets the member's drain_state to draining, then drained. resume sets it to active.

Interface Draining or drained member Readiness Fails. Leadership Moves to another voter. P-CSCF Answers REGISTER with 305 Use Proxy.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No such member. 409 The member is the only member of the cluster. 410 The node was removed from the cluster.

docs.title: Remove a Member
docs.text:
This path removes a drained member from the cluster. The removed node stops serving until its data directory is deleted.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description force boolean true removes a member that is not drained, such as one that is down for good.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No such member. 409 The member is not drained, or the cluster would lose its majority without it. 421 The node is not the leader. See Leader-Only Paths. 503 No leader. Retry.

docs.title: Leader-Only Paths
docs.text:
Remove a Member and Restore run on the leader only. Any other node answers 421, with the leader's API address in leader.

Field Type Description error string The error. leader string API address of the leader. Absent when the leader has none.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "error": "This node is not the cluster leader: send the request to https://10.0.0.1:5020",
    "leader": "https://10.0.0.1:5020"
}

docs.title: Diameter
docs.text: Diameter peers are the HSSs, SLFs, PCRFs, DRAs, SMSCs, MMEs and SMSFs Ella IMS connects to. Routes set the realm the requests of each routed application go to.

docs.title: List Diameter Peers
docs.text:
This path returns the list of Diameter peers, in the order they were created in.

docs.title: Response Fields

The peers of an SMS route are tried by priority. status object Connection to the peer. status.state string down, connecting, open, suspect, reopen or closing. down until the IMS has tried the peer. status.since string Time of the last state change (RFC 3339). status.remote_address string Remote address of the connection. status.host string Origin-Host the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange, else the configured host. status.realm string Origin-Realm the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange. status.error string Why the last connection to the peer failed.

docs.title: Query Parameters

docs.title: Single Sign-On
docs.text: These paths configure sign-in to the UI through an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider. They require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: Get the OIDC Settings
docs.text:
This path never returns the client secret.

Method Path GET /api/v1/oidc

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description enabled boolean Users can sign in through the identity provider. external_url string The URL users reach Ella IMS at. redirect_url string The redirect URL to register at the identity provider. Empty without an external URL. issuer string The identity provider's issuer URL. client_id string The client ID registered at the identity provider. client_secret_set boolean A client secret is stored. display_name string The name on the login button. scopes array The scopes requested. Initially openid, email and profile. session_lifetime_seconds int How long a session started through the identity provider lasts. Initially 86400. trust_unverified_email boolean Email addresses are accepted when the identity provider does not send email_verified. An email_verified of false is always refused. ca_certificate string PEM certificates the identity provider's TLS certificate must chain to. Empty: the system's. groups_claim string The claim, in the ID token or UserInfo, that holds the user's groups. group_roles array Group-to-role mappings, in order.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "external_url": "https://ims.example.com",
        "redirect_url": "https://ims.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback",
        "issuer": "https://idp.example.com/realms/ims",
        "client_id": "ims",
        "client_secret_set": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak",
        "scopes": ["openid", "email", "profile"],
        "session_lifetime_seconds": 86400,
        "trust_unverified_email": false,
        "ca_certificate": "",
        "groups_claim": "groups",
        "group_roles": [
            {"group": "ims-admins", "role_id": 1},
            {"group": "noc", "role_id": 3}
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Update the OIDC Settings
docs.text:
This path replaces the settings, which take effect at once. Disabling OIDC or changing the issuer ends all sessions started through the identity provider.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/oidc

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description enabled boolean Yes external_url string When enabled An https URL with no path. Stored as https://host[:port]. issuer string When enabled An https URL with no query or fragment, as the identity provider gives it. client_id string When enabled At most 255 characters. client_secret string When enabled and none is stored, or when issuer or client_id changes At most 255 characters. Empty or absent: the stored secret is kept. display_name string When enabled At most 64 characters. scopes array Yes At most 20, including openid and email. session_lifetime_seconds int Yes 300 to 2592000 (30 days). trust_unverified_email boolean No Default false. ca_certificate string No PEM certificates. groups_claim string With group_roles The claim name, such as groups. group_roles array No At most 100 objects with a group, matched exactly, and a role_id, 1 to 3. Each group at most once.

docs.title: Group Roles
docs.text: group_roles At each login through the identity provider Empty An Admin sets the role. Someone with no user in Ella IMS is refused. Not empty The first mapping whose group the user is in sets the role. A user in none is refused. Someone with no user in Ella IMS gets one, with that role. A pinned role is kept, whatever the groups. The last Admin with a password stays Admin.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 Updated. The response holds the new settings. 400 Invalid field, or issuer or client_id changes without a client_secret.

docs.title: Test an Identity Provider
docs.text:
This path checks that Ella IMS can use an identity provider. It changes no setting.

Method Path POST /api/v1/oidc/discovery

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description issuer string Yes The issuer URL to test. ca_certificate string No PEM certificates to trust for the provider.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description issuer string The provider's issuer. authorization_endpoint string token_endpoint string token_endpoint_auth_method string client_secret_basic or client_secret_post: how Ella IMS sends the client secret. userinfo_endpoint string Empty if the provider has none. jwks_uri string signing_algorithms array The algorithms the provider signs ID tokens with. keys int The number of signing keys. pkce boolean The provider supports PKCE. issuer_parameter boolean The provider supports RFC 9207.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 The provider can be used. 400 Invalid issuer or CA certificate. 502 The provider cannot be reached or cannot be used, for example because its token endpoint supports neither client_secret_basic nor client_secret_post. The error says why.

docs.title: Operator
docs.text: The operator is the PLMN of the IMS, from which its Diameter identity derives, its home network domain, and the numbering plan that converts dial strings to E.164 numbers.

docs.title: Get the Operator
docs.text:
This path returns the operator settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mcc string Mobile Country Code. mnc string Mobile Network Code. domain string Home network domain name. Empty: ims.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org, with the MNC padded to 3 digits. numbering object Conversion of dial strings to E.164 numbers. numbering.country_code string Country code. numbering.national_prefix string National prefix. numbering.international_prefix string International prefix. numbering.min_national_digits integer Fewest digits a number dialled without a prefix needs to be routed to a SIP trunk. 0: never.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "domain": "",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011",
            "min_national_digits": 7
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Operator
docs.text:
This path replaces the operator settings. A change of MCC, MNC or domain restarts Diameter and SIP under the new names.

The domain derived from the MCC and MNC stays a home domain when domain is set.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description mcc string Yes 3 digits. mnc string Yes 2 or 3 digits. domain string No Domain name of at least two labels, up to 253 characters, stored in lowercase. Under 3gppnetwork.org, only the domain derived from the MCC and MNC. Default empty: derived from the MCC and MNC. numbering object Yes numbering.country_code string Yes 1 to 3 digits, not starting with 0. numbering.national_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits. Differs from international_prefix unless empty. numbering.international_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits. numbering.min_national_digits integer No 0 to 15. Default 7. Fewest digits a number dialled without a prefix needs to be routed to a SIP trunk. 0: never.

docs.text:
{
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "domain": "",
    "numbering": {
        "country_code": "1",
        "national_prefix": "1",
        "international_prefix": "011",
        "min_national_digits": 7
    }
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "domain": "",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011",
            "min_national_digits": 7
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Policy
docs.text: The policy function is the interface the P-CSCF uses for policy control: none, Rx to a PCRF, or N5 to a PCF.

docs.title: Get the Policy
docs.text:
This path returns the policy function settings and the policy function running.

Method Path GET /api/v1/policy

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description interface string none, rx or n5. n5 object Present for the n5 interface only. n5.pcf_uri string API root of the PCF, http[s]://host[:port][/prefix]. status object Policy function running. Differs from the settings while the IMS applies them. status.interface string none, rx or n5. status.endpoint string rx for Rx; the API root of the PCF for N5. status.notify string Address of the N5 notification listener. status.last object Outcome of the last request to the PCF. N5 only. status.last.at string Time of the request (RFC 3339). status.last.reachable boolean Whether the PCF answered. status.last.result string Result of the request.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "interface": "rx",
        "status": {
            "interface": "rx",
            "endpoint": "rx"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Policy
docs.text:
This path replaces the policy function settings. Calls and registrations after the change use the new policy function.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/policy

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description interface string Yes none, rx or n5. n5 requires n5 in the configuration file. n5 object No For the n5 interface only. n5.pcf_uri string Yes http[s]://host[:port][/prefix]. https requires n5.tls in the configuration file, http requires none.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "interface": "none"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "interface": "none",
        "status": {
            "interface": "rx",
            "endpoint": "rx"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Pprof
docs.text: These paths serve the net/http/pprof API. They require Admin, and accept an API token.

docs.title: Profiling Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/v1/pprof/ An HTML page listing the available profiles. GET /api/v1/pprof/allocs A sampling of all past memory allocations. GET /api/v1/pprof/cmdline The command line invocation of the program. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutine Stack traces of all current goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutineleak Stack traces of all leaked goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/heap A sampling of memory allocations of live objects. GET /api/v1/pprof/profile A CPU profile, of 30 seconds by default. GET /api/v1/pprof/threadcreate Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads. GET /api/v1/pprof/trace An execution trace, of 1 second by default. GET, POST /api/v1/pprof/symbol Function names of program counters.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Paths Description seconds profile, trace Duration of the capture. seconds allocs, goroutine, heap Returns the difference of the profile over this duration. debug allocs, goroutine, heap, threadcreate 0: protobuf. 1: text. 2 (goroutine): stack traces in the format of a panic. gc heap 1: runs a garbage collection first.

docs.title: Registrations
docs.text: A registration is a private user identity registered with the S-CSCF, with its registered implicit registration sets.

docs.title: List Registrations
docs.text:
This path returns the list of registered private identities.

Method Path GET /api/v1/registrations

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description search query str Substring of a private or public identity. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description impi string Private user identity. implicit_registration_sets array Registered implicit registration sets of the private identity. A set registers and deregisters as one (TS 23.228 §5.2.1a.0). implicit_registration_sets[].hss object Origin-Host (host) and Origin-Realm (realm) of the last Cx answer for the set. Absent while unknown. implicit_registration_sets[].identities array Public user identities of the set. identities[].uri string Public user identity. identities[].display_name string Display name. Absent if none. identities[].barred boolean Whether the identity is barred. identities[].registered_with array Other private identities a request to this public identity reaches (TS 24.229 §5.4.3.3 step 8). implicit_registration_sets[].contacts array Unexpired contacts bound to the set. A contact bound to several sets is listed in each. contacts[].contact string Contact URI. contacts[].instance string Instance ID, an IMEI URN when available (TS 23.003 §13.8). Absent if none. contacts[].reg_id int reg-id of the flow (RFC 5626). Absent if none. contacts[].q number q-value (RFC 3841 §7.2.3). contacts[].media array Media the device registered for: audio, video. contacts[].registered_at string Registration time (RFC 3339). contacts[].expires_at string Expiry time (RFC 3339). contacts[].address string Address and port of the device, as seen by the P-CSCF. Absent if unknown. contacts[].transport string udp or tcp. Absent if unknown. contacts[].protected boolean Whether IPsec protects the signalling of the device. contacts[].signalling_path string State of the IMS signalling path of the device: unmonitored, monitored or lost.

docs.title: Re-authenticate a Registration
docs.text:
This path brings forward the expiry of the bindings of a registered private identity and has its next REGISTER challenged (TS 24.229 §5.4.1.6).

Method Path POST /api/v1/registrations/{impi}/reauthenticate

docs.title: Path Parameters

docs.title: Response Codes

docs.title: SIP
docs.text: The SIP names of Ella IMS derive from the operator settings.

docs.title: Get SIP Information
docs.text:
This path returns the home domain, the host names the IMS answers to, and the SIP listeners.

docs.title: Create a SIP Trunk
docs.text:
This path creates a SIP trunk.

Method Path POST /api/v1/sip-trunks

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes 1 to 64 printable characters, without leading or trailing spaces. Unique among trunks, ignoring case. addresses array Yes At least one, each once, none reaching the same server as an address of another trunk: the same host, with a port and a transport that can match once their defaults apply. See Addresses and DNS. addresses[].host string Yes Domain name, or specific IPv4 or IPv6 address. addresses[].port int No 1–65535. addresses[].transport string No udp, tcp or tls. tls needs tls.ca_certificates or tls.pins. inbound_cidrs array No Networks, such as 198.51.100.0/24, or single addresses. No two may overlap, in this trunk or across trunks. None may overlap sip.addresses or sip.trusted_networks of the configuration file. Not 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. Default: the IP addresses among the hosts of addresses. domain string No Domain name, or specific IPv4 or IPv6 address, without brackets. Default: the first domain name among the hosts of addresses. Required if every host is an IP address. trusted boolean No Default false. A trusted trunk never uses UDP: no address may have udp as transport. keepalive_interval int No 5–3600 seconds, or 0 for no OPTIONS requests. Default 30. enabled boolean No Default true. tls object No Absent for a trunk without TLS. See TLS. tls.required boolean No Default false. Every address must have tls as transport. Requires ibcf.external.tls in the configuration file. tls.ca_certificates string No PEM-encoded CA certificates, at most 32. tls.pins array No At most 32, each a PEM-encoded certificate, or a SHA-256 fingerprint as 32 hex bytes, with or without colons. tls.identities array No Domain names, at most 16. Default: domain and the domain names among the hosts of addresses. Required with tls.ca_certificates if there are none.

docs.title: Addresses and DNS
docs.text:
host transport port Requests go to Domain name — — The NAPTR, then SRV, then A and AAAA records of the domain. Domain name Set — The SRV records for that transport, else the A and AAAA records at the default port. Domain name Set or — Set The A and AAAA records, at that port, over that transport, else UDP. IP address Set or — Set or — That address, at that port, else the default port, over that transport, else UDP.

The default port is 5060 for udp and tcp, and 5061 for tls. A trusted trunk skips UDP records, and uses TCP instead of UDP.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text:
Carrier authenticated by Field Carrier's certificate must hold A CA tls.ca_certificates One of tls.identities Its own certificate tls.pins One of tls.identities, unless the address is an IP address

An identity is the host of a sip URI or a DNS name in the certificate's subjectAltName, or its common name if it has none.

TLS connection opened by Extended key usage of each certificate of the carrier's chain, if present Ella IMS serverAuth, anyExtendedKeyUsage or id-kp-sipDomain The carrier clientAuth, anyExtendedKeyUsage or id-kp-sipDomain

With tls.required, the carrier must use TLS, and present a certificate on the TLS connections it opens.

CA certificates and PEM pins must not be expired when added. Ella IMS keeps the fingerprint of a PEM pin only.

Ella IMS's own certificate is ibcf.external.tls in the configuration file.

docs.text: Code Description 400 A field is invalid, an inbound network overlaps the networks of the configuration file, or tls.required is set without ibcf.external.tls. 409 Another trunk has the same name, an address that reaches the same server as one of this trunk's, or an inbound network that overlaps one of this trunk's.

This path sets the role of a user. A role change ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot change its own role, and the last Admin with a password stays an Admin.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description role_id int Yes 1 to 3. role_pinned boolean No Keep the role whatever the user's groups. Without it, the current value is kept.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 409 The role comes from the user's groups and role_pinned is not true, or the user is the last Admin with a password.

docs.title: Update a User's Password
docs.text:
This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}/password

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes.

docs.title: Remove a User's Password
docs.text:
This path removes the password of a user, who can then sign in only through the identity provider. It ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot remove its own password, and the last Admin with a password keeps it.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/password

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 409 The user has no password, or is the last Admin with a password.

docs.title: Unlink a User
docs.text:
This path unlinks a user from their account at the identity provider, and ends the sessions started through it. Their next login through the identity provider links them again by email. An Admin cannot unlink itself.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/oidc

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No user has the email, or the user is not linked to the current identity provider.

docs.title: Delete a User
docs.text:
This path deletes the user with its sessions and API tokens. An Admin cannot delete itself, and the last Admin with a password cannot be deleted.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 409 The user is the last Admin with a password.

docs.title: Create an API Token
docs.text:
This path returns the token, the only time it is shown. At most 12 per user. Requires an access token.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens POST /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes 3 to 50 characters, unique among the user's tokens. expires_at string No RFC 3339 time in the future. Without it, the token does not expire.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 Created. 400 Invalid field, or 12 tokens exist. 409 The user has a token of that name.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "name": "Monitoring",
    "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00Z"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellaims_aB3dE5fG7hJ9_KQ4ZN2X7WJ5R3TQY6PLM2VA4CF"
    }
}

docs.title: List API Tokens
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens GET /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Token identifier: the part of the token between ellaims_ and the next _. name string Name. created_at string Creation time. expires_at string Expiry time. Absent for a token that does not expire. last_used_at string Time of the last use, to the minute. Absent for a token never used.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "aB3dE5fG7hJ9",
                "name": "Monitoring",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00.000Z",
                "last_used_at": "2026-10-27T19:02:00.000Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Delete an API Token
docs.text: Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens/{id} DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens/{id}

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
These tutorials walk you through Ella IMS, from your first voice call to running it on Kubernetes.

Tutorial Hardware Required Installation Method Duration Make Your First Voice Call An Ella Core 5G network, a second Linux host, two phones Snap ~30 min Run a High Availability Cluster in the Cloud None, a Google Cloud project or an AWS account Kubernetes ~45 min

docs.title: Make Your First Voice Call
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add Ella IMS to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and make a voice call (VoNR) between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 30 minutes completing this tutorial.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
To complete this tutorial, you will need the following:

Ella Core

  • A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware) tutorial. In this tutorial, Ella Core's N6 interface, ens3, has the address 10.6.0.2.

Ella IMS

  • A second Linux machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, on Ella Core's N6 network. In this tutorial, it has the address 10.6.0.5.

Phones

  • Two 5G phones that support VoNR, each with a SIM provisioned as a subscriber in Ella Core.

docs.title: 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core
docs.text:
On the Ella Core machine, edit the configuration file:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml

Under interfaces, add the address Ella Core accepts Diameter connections on:

/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.6.0.2"

Restart Ella Core:

sudo snap restart ella-core.cored

docs.title: 2. Install Ella IMS
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS machine, install the Ella IMS snap:

sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control

Edit the configuration file:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml

Set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from:

/var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.6.0.5

Start Ella IMS:

sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd

docs.title: 3. Initialize Ella IMS
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to http://10.6.0.5:5020/. The Initialize Ella IMS page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click Create. You should see Ella IMS's Cores page.

docs.title: 4. Connect Ella IMS to Ella Core
docs.text:
Go to the Cores page:

  • Under Peers, click Add Peer, enter 10.6.0.2, check HSS and PCRF, and click Add.
  • Under HSS, click the edit icon next to HSS Realm, enter epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.
  • Under Voice QoS, click the edit icon next to Policy Function, select PCRF, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to PCRF Realm, enter epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.

Under Peers, Ella Core should show as open.

docs.title: 5. Route the phones' traffic
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS machine, route the phones' voice addresses, which we create in the next step, through Ella Core:

sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400

docs.title: 6. Prepare Ella Core for voice
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to the Operator page and scroll to the IMS section. Click the edit icon next to P-CSCF Addresses, enter 10.6.0.5, and click Update.

Go to the Networking page and open the Data Networks tab. Click Create, enter ims as the Name, 10.46.0.0/16 as the IPv4 Pool, turn on IMS (voice and mission critical services), and click Create.

Go to the Profiles page and click on the default profile. Click Add Policy, enter voice as the Name, set the Data Network to ims, and click Create.

Go to the Subscribers page. For each of the two subscribers, click on it, click the edit icon next to MSISDN, enter a number, and click Update:

  • First subscriber: +15551230001
  • Second subscriber: +15551230002

docs.title: 7. Register the phones
docs.text:
On each phone, turn on VoNR, then turn airplane mode on and off.

In Ella IMS, go to the Registrations page. You should see both phones.

docs.title: 8. Make a call
docs.text:
From the first phone, call +15551230002. Answer on the second phone, talk, and hang up.

In Ella IMS, go to the Calls page. You should see the call, with the outcome answered.

Success

Congratulations! You have made a voice call over your private 5G network, through Ella Core and Ella IMS.

docs.title: Run a High Availability Cluster in the Cloud
Run a High Availability Cluster in the Cloud
docs.text:
In this tutorial, you run Ella IMS as a three-node cluster on managed Kubernetes, and watch it survive the loss of a node and a rolling restart.

Note

This tutorial uses managed Kubernetes. Ella IMS can also run as a cluster on cloud virtual machines, installed as a snap, as in Deploy a High Availability Cluster.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
Google CloudAWS
  • A Google Cloud project and the gcloud CLI with the gke-gcloud-auth-plugin component
  • kubectl and git.
  • An AWS account and the aws CLI
  • eksctl, kubectl and git.

docs.title: 1. Create a Kubernetes cluster
docs.text:
Google CloudAWS 
gcloud container clusters create ella-ims \
  --zone us-central1-a \
  --machine-type e2-standard-2 \
  --num-nodes 1 \
  --enable-dataplane-v2 \
  --enable-ip-alias \
  --enable-multi-networking
gcloud container clusters get-credentials ella-ims --zone us-central1-a

Create cluster.yaml:

apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
metadata:
  name: ella-ims
  region: us-east-1
availabilityZones: [us-east-1a, us-east-1b]
addons:
  - name: vpc-cni
    configurationValues: '{"enableNetworkPolicy":"true"}'
  - name: eks-pod-identity-agent
  - name: aws-ebs-csi-driver
    useDefaultPodIdentityAssociations: true
    configurationValues: '{"defaultStorageClass":{"enabled":true}}'
managedNodeGroups:
  - name: ella-ims
    instanceType: t3.medium
    desiredCapacity: 3
    availabilityZones: [us-east-1a]

Create the cluster:

eksctl create cluster -f cluster.yaml

docs.title: 2. Create the SIP network
docs.text:
Google CloudAWS 
gcloud compute networks create ims-sip --subnet-mode custom
gcloud compute networks subnets create ims-sip \
  --network ims-sip \
  --region us-central1 \
  --range 10.60.0.0/24
gcloud compute firewall-rules create ims-sip-allow-internal \
  --network ims-sip \
  --allow esp,udp,tcp,icmp \
  --source-ranges 10.60.0.0/24

export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
VPC=$(aws eks describe-cluster --name ella-ims --query cluster.resourcesVpcConfig.vpcId --output text)
SUBNET=$(aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $VPC \
  --availability-zone us-east-1a \
  --cidr-block 192.168.128.0/24 \
  --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=ims-sip}]' \
  --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text)
SG=$(aws ec2 create-security-group --vpc-id $VPC \
  --group-name ims-sip \
  --description "Ella IMS SIP" \
  --query GroupId --output text)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $SG --protocol all --cidr 192.168.128.0/24

docs.title: 3. Connect the nodes to the SIP network
docs.text:
Google CloudAWS

Create three nodes with a second NIC on the SIP subnet. Each Ella IMS node runs on one of them, with that NIC as eth1:

gcloud container node-pools create ims-sip \
  --cluster ella-ims \
  --zone us-central1-a \
  --machine-type e2-standard-2 \
  --num-nodes 3 \
  --image-type UBUNTU_CONTAINERD \
  --additional-node-network network=ims-sip,subnetwork=ims-sip

Give each node a second NIC on the SIP subnet. Each Ella IMS node runs on one of them, with that NIC as eth1:

for i in $(aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --filters Name=tag:eks:cluster-name,Values=ella-ims Name=instance-state-name,Values=running \
  --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId' --output text); do
  ENI=$(aws ec2 create-network-interface --subnet-id $SUBNET --groups $SG \
    --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=network-interface,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=ims-sip},{Key=node.k8s.amazonaws.com/no_manage,Value=true}]' \
    --query NetworkInterface.NetworkInterfaceId --output text)
  aws ec2 attach-network-interface --network-interface-id $ENI --instance-id $i --device-index 2
done

Install Multus, which gives the NIC to the pod:

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multus-cni/v4.3.1/deployments/multus-daemonset-thick.yml
kubectl rollout status daemonset/kube-multus-ds -n kube-system

docs.title: 4. Deploy Ella IMS
docs.text:
Google CloudAWS 
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
kubectl create secret generic ella-ims-cluster -n ella --from-literal=secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
kubectl apply -k ims/k8s/examples/gke-ha
kubectl get pods -n ella --watch

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
kubectl create secret generic ella-ims-cluster -n ella --from-literal=secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
kubectl apply -k ims/k8s/examples/eks-ha
kubectl get pods -n ella --watch

Wait until the three pods are Running, then press Ctrl+C.

docs.title: 5. Initialize Ella IMS
docs.text:
kubectl port-forward -n ella pod/ella-ims-0 5020:5020

Open http://localhost:5020 and create the first user.

docs.title: 6. Look at the cluster
docs.text:
Open the Cluster page. It names the leader. Only the leader shows the health of the nodes: if ella-ims-0 is not the leader, stop the port-forward with Ctrl+C, and start it again on the leader's pod:

kubectl port-forward -n ella pod/ella-ims-<n> 5020:5020

On the leader's Cluster page, the three nodes appear as Healthy, each with its own Diameter Host.

docs.title: 7. Lose a node
docs.text:
In another terminal, delete the leader's pod:

kubectl delete pod -n ella ella-ims-<n>

The port-forward stops with the pod. Start it again on another pod, and open the Cluster page: another node is the leader. Open the new leader's page as in step 6. The deleted pod comes back, and its node returns to Healthy with the same Diameter Host.

docs.title: 8. Restart the nodes one at a time
docs.text:
Stop the port-forward, then:

kubectl rollout restart statefulset/ella-ims -n ella
kubectl rollout status statefulset/ella-ims -n ella

Open the leader's Cluster page as in step 6: all three nodes are Healthy.

docs.title: 9. Clean up
docs.text:
Google CloudAWS 
kubectl delete statefulset ella-ims -n ella --wait
kubectl wait --for=delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ella-ims -n ella --timeout=2m
kubectl delete -k ims/k8s/examples/gke-ha --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete pvc -n ella --all
kubectl wait --for=delete pv --all --timeout=5m
gcloud container clusters delete ella-ims --zone us-central1-a
gcloud compute firewall-rules delete ims-sip-allow-internal
gcloud compute networks subnets delete ims-sip --region us-central1
gcloud compute networks delete ims-sip

kubectl delete statefulset ella-ims -n ella --wait
kubectl wait --for=delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ella-ims -n ella --timeout=2m
kubectl delete -k ims/k8s/examples/eks-ha --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete pvc -n ella --all
kubectl wait --for=delete pv --all --timeout=5m
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
for ENI in $(aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=ims-sip \
  --query 'NetworkInterfaces[].NetworkInterfaceId' --output text); do
  aws ec2 detach-network-interface --attachment-id $(aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces \
    --network-interface-ids $ENI --query 'NetworkInterfaces[0].Attachment.AttachmentId' --output text)
  aws ec2 wait network-interface-available --network-interface-ids $ENI
  aws ec2 delete-network-interface --network-interface-id $ENI
done
aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id $(aws ec2 describe-security-groups \
  --filters Name=group-name,Values=ims-sip --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' --output text)
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $(aws ec2 describe-subnets \
  --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=ims-sip --query 'Subnets[0].SubnetId' --output text)
eksctl delete cluster -f cluster.yaml --wait
